findings.title: New TotalDocs() log call can crash the process via unsynchronized map iteration
findings.body:
The new log line calls `s.search.TotalDocs()`. By then the goroutine at lines 207-213 is already consuming watch events. `bleveBackend.TotalDocs` (bleve.go:146) ranges over `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu`.

A watch event for a namespace that has no index yet goes through `handleEvent` -> `getOrCreateIndex` -> `BuildIndex`, which writes `b.cache[key]` under `cacheMu.Lock()`. That write can overlap with the lock-free iteration in `TotalDocs`. Concurrent map iteration and write is a fatal Go runtime error, so it crashes the process; it is not a recoverable panic.

The window is roughly as long as `DocCount()` takes across all indexes. Namespaces skipped at startup because they are below `initMinSize` make this path reachable.

Fix: have `TotalDocs` take `cacheMu.RLock()`, or compute the total before starting the watch goroutine.

findings.title: Stop() no longer prevents requests from being served after shutdown
findings.body:
Before this PR, every handler (Create, Read, List, Watch, Search, IsHealthy, blob calls, etc.) called `s.Init(ctx)` and returned `s.initErr`. Since the `sync.Once` had already run, that meant returning whatever `Stop()` had stored ("service is stopping" / "service is stopped").

This PR removes all those calls, so `Stop()` writing `s.initErr` no longer has any effect. After `Stop()` cancels the server context and stops the backend lifecycle, handlers keep running against a stopped backend and a cancelled broadcaster. Callers no longer get a clear "service is stopped" error.

Fix: add an explicit stopped/ready check in the handlers, or have `Stop` close the gRPC service, instead of relying on the now-unused `initErr`.

findings.title: Index-build goroutines race on shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed`, so errors can be lost
findings.body:
Each goroutine started by `group.Go` does `totalBatchesIndexed++` and `_, _, err = s.build(...)`; `return err`. Both variables are the outer function's locals and are shared by all workers.

Before this PR, `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` held `cacheMu` for its whole body, which largely serialized builds. With the lock narrowed, the builds now run truly in parallel. Two consequences:
- The race detector will flag it.
- One goroutine can overwrite another's error with nil before it is returned. A failed namespace build can then be silently dropped instead of failing startup as the comment on `init` promises.
- `namespaced_indexed` will be miscounted.

Fix: use a goroutine-local `err :=` and an `atomic.Int64` for the counter.

findings.title: Narrowed lock lets concurrent builds of the same key run in parallel and overwrite each other
findings.body:
`getOrCreateIndex` checks `GetIndex` and then calls `BuildIndex` with no per-key guard. With the function-wide lock removed, a Search request and a watch event for the same uncached key can build two indexes at once.

The last `b.cache[key] = idx` wins. Any watch-event writes already applied to the losing index are discarded. `IndexTenants` is also incremented twice. For file-backed indexes, the second `bleve.New` on the same directory fails.

Fix: re-check the cache under the write lock before storing, or use a per-key singleflight so finer-grained locking does not introduce lost updates.

findings.title: Failed Init in constructor leaks the cancel func and the already-initialized backend
findings.body:
When `s.Init(ctx)` fails, `NewResourceServer` returns `nil, err` without calling `cancel()` or `s.lifecycle.Stop`.

If `lifecycle.Init` succeeded (for example, the DB connection was opened) and then `search.init` or `initWatcher` failed, the backend's resources and any pollers started are never cleaned up. The caller has no handle to clean them up either, because the server is returned as nil.

The same error is also logged twice: once inside `Init` and again here.

findings.title: Integration test skipped for postgres instead of fixed, possibly masking a regression from eager init
findings.body:
This PR makes unified storage initialize (DB init, full index build, watchers) synchronously inside `NewResourceServer`, which changes storage-server startup behavior. In the same PR, the only module-server integration test is disabled for postgres with "not working in Drone. Works locally."

If the failure is caused by the new eager initialization (for example, slower startup or blocking DB init beyond the 500ms sleep), skipping the test hides exactly the regression the PR description asks reviewers about. Nothing else in the PR adds coverage for the new init-at-construction behavior.
